Interval

/IN-tur-ul/ — three syllables, stress on first · noun

Hear It

What It Means

An interval is a gap or pause in time between two events.

That interval felt endless as she stood alone beneath the humming lights, listening to water drip somewhere in the tunnel.

Worked Example

The concert's second act began after the interval, when the orchestra returned to the stage and musicians retook their seats.

Interval is more precise than the plain word 'break' because it specifically names the gap between two separate events (the end of the first act and the start of the second), not just any pause. The context here — two performances separated by time — is exactly where interval shines.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

gap: A gap is any opening or empty space — a gap in a fence, a gap in your knowledge — and only sometimes involves time. An interval is specifically a stretch of time between two events, and it is often measured exactly. Every interval is a kind of gap, but only the timed, between-events kind.

lull: A lull is a calm, quiet spell inside ongoing activity — a lull in the fighting, a lull in conversation — stressing the quiet itself. An interval is the neutral, often measured stretch of time separating two events; it says nothing about calm. A lull soothes; an interval merely separates.

interlude: An interlude is the episode that fills the time between two parts of something — a musical interlude between acts, a peaceful interlude between crises. Interval names the empty, measured stretch itself rather than what happens during it. The orchestra plays the interlude; the stopwatch measures the interval.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

continuity: unbroken connected flow without any gaps

constancy: steady persistence that never pauses or stops

Where it sits · how precisely the time gap is defined — pause → break → interval

pause vs. interval: A storyteller's pause is just a momentary stop for effect within one activity; interval is the stronger, more precise word for a measurable gap separating two distinct events, like the timed darkness between a lighthouse's flashes.

break vs. interval: A worker's coffee break is an informal rest from a single task; interval makes the stronger, more exact claim of a defined stretch separating two separate events, like the scheduled gap between a hospital's day and night shifts.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — inter-

Prefix — inter-: between, among

Root — vall-

Root — vall-: wall, rampart, palisade (Latin vallum)

Put it together

Put it together: Inter- (between) + vall- (wall, rampart — Latin vallum) builds the meaning literally: the space between the walls. Roman military camps kept an open gap between their tents and their defensive ramparts, and intervallum came to mean any gap at all — first in space, then in time. So the real root here is the wall; inter- is the prefix telling you where you are in relation to it.

Use the root in a new word: wall

Use the root in a new word: wall: Our everyday word wall comes straight from Latin vallum -- Anglo-Saxon builders borrowed the Roman word for a rampart -- so an interval really is the space between the walls.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / timekeeping

Interval emphasizes the gap between two separate events or things, while 'pause' is just a stop within one activity. Use interval in formal or technical contexts (like music, sports, or astronomy) when the separation between two distinct things matters. For a simple stop, 'pause' or 'break' is clearer.
